answer: An island market whose agents trace onyx and ivory provenance could divide admission capacity among vetted sponsors. Each sponsor signs key-bound permits totaling at most its fixed quota; validators reject excess allocations and debit a permit before transferring it. Creating aliases cannot enlarge that conserved capacity. A farm must obtain more independent sponsorship through persuasion or bribery, even in parallel. This assumes honest sponsor selection and exact quota accounting; sponsor collusion can defeat it, and newcomers need an accessible sponsor.
